office_does: The three county commissioners adopt the county budget and set county policy; District 3's commissioner is nominated by the district and elected by the whole county.
race_blurb: First-term Commissioner Mike Garza (prefers Republican), elected in 2022 by 58 votes, faces Eleanor Brodahl (prefers Democrat), a 16-year Othello City Council member who calls herself a conservative Democrat; both live in Othello. Both describe a tight county budget; Garza led the district primary 334 to 227.

candidates.summary: First-term Adams County commissioner and Othello insurance agent, formerly on the Othello School Board and the Columbia Basin Health Association board.
highlights: Says every county office, the commissioners included, was told to cut operating costs as spending outpaced revenue [S2]
'Revenues need to exceed our expenditures – it's math' [S2]
Cites jail-remodel funding and irrigation bridges over the East-Lo canal [S1]
Wants growth from job-creating employers rather than housing [S2]

experience.basis: First-term incumbent running on his record in office.

spending.basis: Describes across-the-board cuts to office operating costs and insists revenues exceed expenditures.

candidates.summary: Former 16-year Othello City Council member with 30 years in banking and finance, running as a conservative Democrat focused on fiscal responsibility.
highlights: 'We can't just keep taxing and taxing our citizenry' [S2]
Says the county must 'live within our means' with a tight budget [S2]
Would raise revenue through economic development, existing businesses and grants [S3]
Calls for better communication between the county, Othello and Ritzville [S2]

experience.basis: Runs on a 16-year city-council record and 30 years in finance, though new to county office.

taxes.basis: Opposes further taxation in the current budget climate and looks to growth and grants for revenue.

spending.basis: Fiscal-responsibility framing: protect taxpayer dollars and live within the county's means.
